summary: The Daihatsu Charmant was a subcompact sedan made by Japan's Daihatsu and based on the Toyota Corolla. It began as a 1970s spin-off of the Corolla, tracked that model's changes, and used Toyota inline-four engines of 1.2 to 1.6 litres. It was eventually replaced by the Daihatsu Applause.
one_line: The Daihatsu Charmant was a Corolla-based subcompact sedan from Japan's Daihatsu, powered by Toyota engines and succeeded by the Applause.
key_facts: The Daihatsu Charmant is a subcompact sedan built by Daihatsu of Japan.
The Daihatsu Charmant is based on the Toyota Corolla.
The Daihatsu Applause replaced the Daihatsu Charmant.
The Daihatsu Charmant was originally a spin-off of the Toyota Corolla of the 1970s.
Daihatsu Charmant model changes paralleled those of the Toyota Corolla.
All Daihatsu Charmants were fitted with Toyota inline-four engines.
Daihatsu Charmant engines ranged from 1.2 to 1.6 litres.
The word "charmant" is French for charming.
